77699.subject: Why A ‘Perfect’ Resume Could Hurt Your Chances Of Getting Hired
77699.body:
Forbes Edge

Автор: Forbes


Автор: Forbes

    
    
    Прочитайте цю статтю на LinkedIn, щоб приєднатися до обговорення
Прочитати на LinkedIn
https://www.linkedin.com/comm/pulse/why-perfect-resume-could-hurt-your-chances-getting-hired-vsosc?lipi=urn%3Ali%3Apage%3Aemail_email_series_follow_newsletter_02%3BISvx8%2F35SkSseQclXURDNQ%3D%3D&midToken=AQFTjFOONAfT2w&midSig=1iwjYuSp_vvIo1&trk=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_&trkEmail=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_-null-fz96fz~mt05vbsn~mx-null-null&eid=fz96fz-mt05vbsn-mx
  
A great resume used to stand out to recruiters because it reflected effort, attention to detail, and the ability to communicate your skills effectively. But in today’s AI era, where every resume looks like it was written by a master copywriter, Forbes’ contributor Julia Korn says a “perfect” resume is now a red flag for many hiring managers.  Today, 70% of job seekers use AI to polish their resume, with Gen Z adoption being even higher at 85%, according to data from Hunar.AI. Korn notes that the pressure to use AI to optimize a resume for an Applicant Tracking System (ATS) makes sense, considering many Fortune 500 companies use ATS to screen a resume before a human even lays eyes on the document. But Korn, who teaches leadership at Duke University’s Fuqua School of Business, warns that using AI to perfectly format and keyword stuff your resume could actually backfire.  “In this environment, a ‘perfect’ resume is no longer a stamp of excellence. Instead, it’s a warning sign for recruiters,” Korn writes.  For applicants looking to stand out when perfection can be a trap, Korn advises to follow two important rules: Rule 1: Embrace Strategic Imperfection and Voice “If you wouldn’t say a sentence out loud in a casual networking conversation, don’t write it on the page,” she says.  Rule 2: Use Hyper-Specific Details and Avoid Broad Buzzwords “AI writes in terms of generalized achievements (e.g., “Improved team efficiency”), but [hiring managers] want to know the verifiable, messy reality (“Redesigned the onboarding email sequence, cutting user drop-off by 19% in Q3”),” she says. “This specificity is the ultimate proof of human work.” Read here to learn more about Korn’s tips on how to create a strategically imperfect resume that will get a recruiter’s attention.  — Courtney Connley-Hampton, Careers Staff Writer WORK SMARTER Practical insights and advice from Forbes staff and contributors to help you succeed in your job, accelerate your career and lead smarter. Prepare for your next career move by “firing” yourself once a year, career expert Nirit Cohen says. Take steps like identifying your transferable skills and growing your professional network. 77697.subject: Solana Beats the Bell
77697.body:
View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/eaa70932-7ce4-467e-b338-a662ed575d6a/0xR_NL_Banner_Heading_Wordmark.jpg?t=1776775276)
Caption: 

Today we examine whether tokenized stocks on Solana trade at fair prices, measuring Backpack’s fills against each stock’s live quote as an execution desk would. Seven weeks in, larger trades are already competitive with TradFi, while Solana gains an edge after hours. Yesterday brought a broad risk-off move led by a 5% semiconductor unwind, with crypto’s AI complex and miners hit hardest.

———————————————————————————

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/42e942ec-f31d-4957-8722-a3ac7b121e1e/0xR_NL_Market_Update.png?t=1767631151) [Market Update]
Caption: 

Yesterday saw a broad risk-off led by the AI complex. Bittensor Eco (-5.5%) and Crypto Miners (-5.1%) were the worst sectors, followed by L2 (-3.7%) and AI (-2.7%), while Launchpad (2.2%) was the only sector meaningfully green. Gold (-2.2%) and the NASDAQ 100 (-1.9%) fell alongside crypto.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/7cd4dc72-9642-4dfe-8244-40b7b2bf529f/image.png?t=1787143048)
Caption: 

The driver was a semiconductor unwind rather than anything crypto-specific. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index closed down 5.0%, with memory hit hardest as Micron fell 7.0% and SK Hynix's ADRs dropped 9.2%. Reported drivers included elevated Treasury yields and questions about how the AI buildout is being financed. Crypto's AI-linked sectors traded as high-beta expressions of that move.

The weekly picture is more specific. Crypto Miners fell 9.1%, second worst behind DEXs, while BTC gained 1.7%. The decline was concentrated in HUT (-12.5%), CIFR (-11.9%), CORZ (-9.9%), WULF (-9.4%), and RIOT (-7.9%).

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/f75d840d-91c2-4aa9-93a8-ac7de1807c69/image.png?t=1787143048)
Caption: 

Four of those five are the index's YTD leaders, with HUT up 57.6%, RIOT 33.6%, WULF 22.6%, and CORZ 17.9%, while every name that outperformed on the week is flat or negative on the year. The selling sits where the gains are. CIFR is the exception at -0.7% YTD, which points to something beyond profit-taking. 

Financing is the likeliest candidate. An AI data center under construction can cost [$20B before equipment is installed](https://www.swissre.com/institute/research/sigma-research/sigma-insights-07-2026-insuring-ai-data-centre-risks.html), and lenders want all of that value covered, but [insurers will not write that much](https://www.insurancebusinessmag.com/us/news/property/the-coverage-ceiling-arrives-for-hyperscale-data-centers-579429.aspx) on a single site. Whatever is left uninsu
